sheet-1-1.description: Main part of sheet 1 of the 1906 Sanborn atlas of Nutley, drawn at 200 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right, below a heavy line that separates it from an inset of a woollen mill at the top of the sheet. It covers the north-western corner of the town, between the Bloomfield town line and the canal along the top, where East Passaic Avenue or Canal runs beside the canal, and Bloomfield Avenue along the bottom. Milton Avenue runs from Bloomfield Avenue north to East Passaic Avenue on the west side, and Center Street crosses the eastern edge. The western margin is the line with the Township of Belleville, where Bloomfield Avenue continues as Joralemon. The area is almost all open land. Development is limited to a row of narrow lots and scattered frame dwellings and stables along Milton Avenue, a few houses around Hawthorn Place, Hope Street and Jefferson Street at Bloomfield Avenue, and, in the north-eastern corner, the small grid of Ridge Avenue, Mount Vernon Avenue, Thomas or Clement Avenue and Van Winkle Avenue west of Center Street, with Redman Lane leaving Center Street to the east. Large unbuilt tracts are marked only by their lot numbers. The canal is coloured blue along the whole northern edge. Sheet numbers in the margins refer to sheet 3 and 4 to the south, sheet 2 to the east and sheet 74 of the Belleville section to the south-west.
notes: Center is today Centre Street.

The sheet is drawn schematically at 200 feet to an inch: drawn junction spacing disagrees with today's streets by 10 to 25 m (Jefferson Street lies about 58 m from Milton Avenue along Bloomfield Avenue on the sheet, 86 m today). Placed from four points with an RMSE of about 6 m; low confidence.
Mount Vernon Avenue and Thomas or Clement Avenue as drawn do not match the positions of today's Mount Vernon Street and Clement Street; they were not used for control.

Scale 200 ft to an inch (main part); north-west corner: Milton Ave, Bloomfield Ave, Center, Van Winkle, Ridge, Mount Vernon, Thomas or Clement Aves, East Passaic Ave or Canal. Two parts: part 1 main map below a heavy line; part 2 inset at the top, 50 ft, of the Samuel Lobsitz woollen mill on the Third River at Harrison and John Streets (also drawn on sheet 3).

sheet-1-2.description: Inset at the top of sheet 1 of the 1906 Sanborn atlas of Nutley, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right and separated from the main map below it by a heavy line marked See Volume Two Essex County. It shows the woollen mill of Samuel Lobsitz, manufacturer of garnetted and carded wool and silk, on the Third River west of Harrison Street, at the corner of John Street, in the western part of the town; sheet 3 shows the same works at 100 feet to an inch and refers to this sheet for details. The mill is a large group of brick buildings: picker houses, a drying and scouring room, a wash house, a boiler house with two boilers, and a long carding and garnetting building of two and three storeys, with smaller brick and frame picker houses south of them. Frame and iron-clad store houses, a storage building over the tail race and a closet stand toward the south and east. A head race enters from the west and a tail race leaves the mill to rejoin the Third River, which curves across the western part of the inset. A long note records the watchman, power by steam and water, heating, electric light, the water supply from a tank and the river, the fire pumps and hose. Rights of way of the Newark City water supply and of the East Jersey Water Company cross the south-eastern corner. The western half of the inset is blank, and a scale of feet and a north arrow are drawn near the bottom.
notes: John St. is today Prospect Street (Harrison Street / Prospect Street).

Placed from seven building corners carried from sheet 3 and the Harrison / John junction, hand-picked at the top edge of the sheet; the fitted scale (8.1 px per foot) is about 3 percent larger than 50 feet to an inch on this scan, so sheet 3 may draw the mill slightly small.

Scale 200 ft to an inch (main part); north-west corner: Milton Ave, Bloomfield Ave, Center, Van Winkle, Ridge, Mount Vernon, Thomas or Clement Aves, East Passaic Ave or Canal. Two parts: part 1 main map below a heavy line; part 2 inset at the top, 50 ft, of the Samuel Lobsitz woollen mill on the Third River at Harrison and John Streets (also drawn on sheet 3).

sheet-2-1.description: Lower and larger part of sheet 2 of the 1906 Sanborn atlas of Nutley, drawn at 200 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right, below a heavy line that separates it from the upper part of the sheet. It covers the thinly built north-eastern corner of the town between Coeyman Avenue on the west and the Passaic County line, the boundary with Acquackanonck Township, on the east. Its northern edge is the town line with Bloomfield, along which East Passaic Avenue runs, and its southern edge is Bloomfield Avenue. High Street crosses the part diagonally from Bloomfield Avenue to Joerg Avenue, and Kingsland Road runs north to south in the eastern half. Between them are the newer streets of the period: Joerg Avenue and Kenzel Avenue with Cadmus and Charles Avenue at the northern edge, Alexander Avenue, and New Nutley Avenue with Laura Avenue, Emily Avenue and Stager Place running from it to Bloomfield Avenue. A row of narrow building lots is laid out along Kenzel Avenue, but most blocks hold only scattered frame dwellings and stables, and the large area west of High Street around Steedman Lane is open land. A row of small buildings on Bloomfield Avenue near Kingsland Road is marked for a special sheet, number 24. The Newark Branch of the Erie Railroad crosses the south-eastern corner. Water pipes and hydrants are shown along the built streets. The labels Vreeland and Daily Avenue at the bottom edge belong to streets continued on sheet 7.
notes: New Nutley Avenue is today Edison Avenue.
Stager Place is today Spruce Street; Charles Avenue is today Charles Street.
Kingsland Road on this part is today Kingsland Street.
The High Street / Joerg Avenue junction sat 12.6 m off the fit and was rejected; Kenzel Avenue / Kingsland Street (7 m off) was excluded.
Steedman Lane does not survive under that name; today's Alexander Avenue reaches Coeyman Avenue at a different place.

Scale 200 ft to an inch. Two parts split by a heavy line: part 1 (lower) High St, Kingsland Road (today Kingsland Street), Joerg, Kenzel, Alexander, New Nutley (today Edison), Laura, Emily, Stager Pl (today Spruce St) to Bloomfield Ave; part 2 (upper) Center St to Coeyman Ave north of Bloomfield Ave, mostly open land.

sheet-2-2.description: Upper part of sheet 2 of the 1906 Sanborn atlas of Nutley, drawn at 200 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right, above a heavy line that separates it from the lower part of the sheet. It covers the north-western edge of the town between Center Street on the west and Coeyman Avenue on the east, with Bloomfield Avenue along its southern edge and the town line with Bloomfield, marked See Volume Two Essex County, along the top. East Passaic Avenue, labelled east of Center Street as East Passaic Avenue or Canal, follows the town line, and Ridge Avenue and Van Winkle Avenue meet Center Street from the west. The interior is almost entirely open land crossed by Redman Lane, Chappel Lane, the dashed lines of the proposed Payne street and Davis Avenue in the north. A wide right of way of the Newark City water supply and of the East Jersey Water Company runs diagonally across the part from the north-east to the south-west. Buildings are few and scattered: frame dwellings with stables and a workshop near Center Street and Redman Lane, and a handful of houses near Payne and Davis Avenue at the northern edge. Along Bloomfield Avenue the short ends of Church Street, Bank Street, Mountain View Avenue and Beech Street are drawn running south to the dividing line, where sheets 5 and 6 continue them. A large compass rose stands in the open land near the west.
notes: Center is today Centre Street; Mountain View Avenue is today Mountainview Avenue.

Placed by a Helmert transformation from two junctions (Center / Bloomfield Avenue and Bloomfield / Coeyman Avenue, about 1 km apart); Center / Van Winkle Avenue sat about 10 m off and was left out. Low confidence.
Ridge Avenue as drawn, north of Van Winkle Avenue, does not match today's Ridge Road, which meets Centre Street south of Van Winkle Avenue.
Right of way of the Newark City water supply and of the East Jersey Water Company crosses the part.

Scale 200 ft to an inch. Two parts split by a heavy line: part 1 (lower) High St, Kingsland Road (today Kingsland Street), Joerg, Kenzel, Alexander, New Nutley (today Edison), Laura, Emily, Stager Pl (today Spruce St) to Bloomfield Ave; part 2 (upper) Center St to Coeyman Ave north of Bloomfield Ave, mostly open land.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 of the 1906 Sanborn atlas of Nutley, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, with north toward the upper right. It covers the north-western corner of the town along the Belleville boundary, whose line (Township of Belleville) runs as a dash-dot line from the top left to the bottom of the sheet. Bloomfield Avenue crosses the top of the sheet from left to right. Hope Street, Jefferson Street and Brown Street are laid out between Bloomfield Avenue and the open land to the south: a few frame dwellings and outbuildings stand along Bloomfield Avenue and Jefferson Street, and a few buildings stand near Brown Street; one building on Bloomfield Avenue is coloured blue and pink. Harrison Street forms the east edge of the sheet and Franklin Avenue the bottom edge. Rutan Place crosses the open ground as a long, narrow strip, and a few dwellings and barns stand in fields along it. The Third River winds across the lower half of the sheet from the left edge to the lower right; at the right edge stand the buildings of the Samuel Lobsitz woollen mill, drawn in pink as brick and marked as garnetted and carded wool and silk, with a reference to sheet 1 for details, together with sheds and a dwelling. Beyond the mill the river divides around an island. A straight channel runs from the left edge toward the mill. The rights of way of the Newark City Water Supply and the East Jersey Water Company cross the lower right corner diagonally with pipe lines, and E. Unger's chicken farm with several coops stands south of the river. A compass rose and the scale bar are printed in the lower part. Most of the sheet is open farmland. Adjoining sheets are numbered 1 to the north, 4 to the east and 9 to the south, and 74 to the west.
notes: John St. at the right edge, where it meets Harrison Street, is today Prospect Street (Harrison Street / Prospect Street, 298 m south-east of Brown Street along Harrison Street).
Hope, Jefferson and Brown are today Hope Street, Jefferson Street and Brown Street; Milton is today Milton Avenue, which meets Bloomfield Avenue and Hope Street.
Rutan Place is drawn as a long narrow strip across the open ground; no junction on it was used for control.
The Samuel Lobsitz mill is drawn again at larger scale on sheet 1; the printed reference is 'For details see sheet No. 1'.

Scale 100 ft. Bloomfield Ave, Hope, Jefferson, Brown, Harrison, Rutan Pl, Franklin; Samuel Lobsitz woollen mill and Third River at the right edge (details on sheet 1, part 2); John St. is today Prospect Street. One part.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 of the 1906 Sanborn atlas of Nutley, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, with north toward the upper right. It shows a thinly built district in the north-west of the town, bounded on the north by Bloomfield Avenue, on the west by Harrison Street, on the east by Center Street and on the south by Franklin Avenue. John Street crosses the middle of the sheet from Harrison Street to Center Street. Most of the sheet is open land. A small row of frame dwellings stands on the east side of Harrison Street north of Brown Street, a few dwellings and outbuildings lie along Bloomfield Avenue, and the farm of A. Rusby, with a dwelling and sheds, sits in the open ground west of the middle. Lots lettered A to H front Harrison Street south of John Street and Franklin Avenue, and a handful of dwellings stand on the south side of the sheet. South of John Street Chase, Locust, Stager, Race and Woodland Avenue are laid out with dashed lines as proposed streets and are not built. A stream, a branch of the Third River, enters from the north-east, widens into a pond near the top right, and passes under John Street and across the lower part of the sheet. Two rights of way for water mains, one of the Newark City Water Supply and one of the East Jersey Water Company, cross the sheet diagonally from the lower left to the upper right, drawn as broken parallel lines with pipe sizes. Water pipes of 6 inches are marked along Franklin Avenue and Harrison Street. Neighbouring sheets are numbered 1 to the north, 3 to the west, 5 to the east and 9 to the south.
notes: John Street is today Prospect Street (it meets Harrison Street 298 m from Brown Street); its junction with Harrison Street was hand-picked.
Center is today Centre Street; Brown St. is Brown Street, still named.

Chase, Locust, Stager, Race and Woodland Avenue north of Franklin Avenue are drawn dashed as proposed streets; Chase Street, Stager Street, Race Street and Woodland Avenue exist today, Locust Street too.
Stager Street and Franklin Place south of Franklin Avenue are drawn dashed at the bottom edge and belong to sheet 9.
Printed sheet number 4; scale bar reads 100 feet to one inch.
Scale 100 ft. Bloomfield Ave, Harrison, Brown, John (Prospect Street), Center (Centre Street), Franklin; Chase, Locust, Stager, Race, Woodland dashed. One part.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 of the 1906 Sanborn atlas of Nutley, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, with north toward the upper right. It shows the old village centre in the north-west of the town, bounded on the north by Bloomfield Avenue, on the west by Center Street, on the east by Mountain View Avenue and on the south by Franklin Avenue. Church Street runs diagonally from Bloomfield Avenue to a junction with John Street and Prospect, and on to Franklin Avenue. John Street enters from the west edge and Prospect continues east from Church Street to Mountain View Avenue, with Chestnut running south-east from Prospect to Franklin Avenue. Old Valley Rd. cuts across the north side between Church Street and Bank. The village frontage is closely built with frame dwellings along Church Street, Prospect and Mountain View Avenue, with a school marked as the Church St. School (drawn in pink as brick) and the Protestant Reformed Dutch Church with its cemetery on the east side of Church Street. Rows of lettered house lots front Church Street, the south side of John Street and Franklin Avenue, where a few shops, flats and a restaurant are marked. Much of the north-western part is still farmland. Bank, Plane, West, Division, Melvina, Broadbent Pl. and the northern part of Chestnut are drawn with dashed lines as proposed streets. Two water-main rights of way (Newark City Water Supply and East Jersey Water Co.) run diagonally across the upper left, with a compass rose below them. Water pipes of 5 and 6 inches are marked along Franklin Avenue. Adjoining sheets are numbered 2 to the north, 4 to the west, 6 to the east, 11 and 12 to the south.
notes: John (west of Church) and Prospect (east of Church) are today both Prospect Street; the street jogs about 40 m at Church Street, matching the two OpenStreetMap nodes of Church Street / Prospect Street.
Center is today Centre Street; Mountain View Avenue is today Mountainview Avenue.
Prospect Street / William Street (modern) is not drawn: William Street appears only south of Franklin Avenue, and that junction was excluded.
Bank, Plane, West, Division, Melvina and the north part of Chestnut are drawn dashed as proposed streets; Old Valley Road, Broadbent Place and Melvina Street are not in the OpenStreetMap extract.
Control points run 3 to 5 m from the fit, suggesting the sheet is drawn slightly off the modern street grid.
Scale 100 ft. Village centre: Church, John/Prospect, Chestnut, Mountain View, Franklin, Old Valley Rd; Bank, Plane, West, Division, Melvina dashed. One part.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 of the 1906 Sanborn atlas of Nutley, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, with this sheet turned so that north points toward the upper right at a steeper angle than on sheets 4 and 5. It covers the area north-east of the village centre between Bloomfield Avenue along the top, Chestnut on the west, Franklin Avenue along the bottom and Vreeland Avenue on the east. Mountain View Ave. and Beech run from Bloomfield Avenue south to Prospect, which crosses the sheet from the upper left to the right edge. South of Prospect, Hillside Ave. runs parallel to it on a long curve to its junction with Vreeland Avenue. The blocks along Prospect and Hillside Avenue are divided into long narrow house lots lettered A to Q, with frame dwellings built on some of them, and a few houses stand along Beech and Bloomfield Avenue. The large blocks between Mountain View Ave., Beech and Coeyman, and most of the north-eastern part of the sheet, are open ground. Bank, Plane St., Chestnut St. (north of Prospect), Division St. and Coeyman are drawn with dashed lines as proposed streets with no buildings; Old Valley Rd. appears in the upper left corner. At the right edge Vreeland Ave. crosses the end of Prospect and Hillside Ave., and a short street named Colonial Terrace branches off it. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches are marked along Mountain View Ave., Chestnut, Franklin Avenue and Vreeland Ave. A compass rose is printed in the northern part. Adjoining sheets are numbered 2 to the north, 5 to the west, 7 to the east and 12 to the south.
notes: Mountain View Avenue is today Mountainview Avenue; Beech is today Beech Street, Chestnut is Chestnut Street, Prospect is Prospect Street.

Bloomfield Avenue was not used for control: its modern junctions with Mountainview Avenue and Beech Street lie about 11 to 13 m (about 3 percent of the street length) beyond where the sheet draws them, so the modern street is probably widened or shifted.
Chestnut Street / Prospect Street (modern) lies about 15 m east of the drawn corner, so the realigned north end of Chestnut Street was not used.
Coeyman, Bank, Plane Street, Division Street and the north part of Chestnut Street are drawn dashed as proposed streets.
Scale 100 ft, rotation about 73. Bloomfield, Mountain View, Beech, Prospect, Hillside, Vreeland, Chestnut; Bloomfield Ave junctions 11-13 m off, top third uncontrolled. One part.

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 of the 1906 Sanborn atlas of Nutley, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. It covers a residential district in the north-central part of the town, bounded on the north by Bloomfield Avenue, on the east by High Street, on the south by Hillside Avenue and on the west by Coeyman Avenue. Vreeland Avenue runs north to south through the western half of the sheet, and Prospect Street crosses the whole sheet from west to east. Between Vreeland Avenue and Bloomfield Avenue the short streets Sylvan Place and Oak Crest Place are laid out with a few houses, while Coeyman Avenue, Daily Avenue and the northern part of Vreeland Avenue are drawn only with dashed lines as proposed streets with no buildings along them. South of Prospect Street, Hawthorn Avenue and Colonial Terrace are lined with recently built frame dwellings on narrow lots, and the blocks along High Street are subdivided into regular house lots. The buildings are almost all one- and two-storey frame dwellings with a few sheds and an auto shed; there is no commercial or industrial building on the sheet. Water pipes are noted along the built streets with their diameters, and hydrants are marked. In the south-eastern corner the tracks of the railroad cross the sheet diagonally near West Nutley Plaza and Hillside Avenue. Large parts of the sheet, especially the north-west between Coeyman Avenue and Vreeland Avenue and the area south of Colonial Terrace near Hillside Avenue, are still open land. Adjoining sheet numbers are printed in the margins: 2 to the north, 6 to the west, 8 to the east and 13 to the south.
notes: Hawthorn Avenue is today Hawthorne Avenue; its junctions sat 3 to 4 m off the fit and were left out of the control.
Oak Crest Place is today Oakcrest Place; its junction with Vreeland Avenue sat about 6 m off and was left out.
Daily Avenue is today Daily Street; Funston Street is today Funston Place.
Coeyman Avenue, Daily Avenue and Vreeland Avenue north of Sylvan Place are drawn dashed, as proposed streets.

Scale 100 ft. Bloomfield Ave, High St, Vreeland Ave, Prospect, Hawthorn Ave, Colonial Terrace, Hillside Ave, Sylvan Pl, Oak Crest Pl; Coeyman and Daily Aves dashed (paper streets). Pilot sheet. One part.

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 of the 1906 Sanborn atlas of Nutley, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. It lies east of sheet 7 and covers the north-eastern edge of the town along the Passaic County line. Bloomfield Avenue crosses the top, High Street bounds the west edge, Hillside Avenue crosses the bottom and Orange Street, beside the line between Acquackanonck Township and Passaic County, bounds the east edge. Kingsland Road runs diagonally down the sheet beside the Erie Railroad's Newark Branch, whose tracks cross from the upper right to the lower left. Along the railroad stand the X Ray Stove Polish Co. on the Pond fed by the Third River, and Geo. La Monte and Son, makers of safety paper; both works are drawn in colour and carry a note referring to detail on another sheet. In the lower left the Nutley Coal and Supply Co. has a yard and sheds beside the tracks. The only dense building is in the lower right, where houses line Cathedral Avenue, Terrace Avenue and Glendale along a half-laid-out grid. Elsewhere the sheet is largely open land: the blocks between High Street and the railroad hold a few frame dwellings and a city hose cart house, and a large block marked Oakland Avenue on the east side is empty. Several streets are drawn dashed as proposed, including Cedar. A watercourse winds through the middle of the sheet. The scale bar and the compass rose are printed on the sheet, and the sheet number 8 is at the upper right, with the neighbouring sheets 2, 7 and 14 numbered at the margins.
notes: Stager Place is today Spruce Street; Funston is today Funston Place.
Kingsland Road as drawn runs about 40 m from today's Kingsland Street line, so Kingsland Street was left out of the control.
The X Ray Stove Polish Co. and Geo. La Monte and Son works are noted as shown in detail on another sheet.

Scale 100 ft. North-east corner on the Passaic County line: Bloomfield Ave, Stager Pl (Spruce Street), Kingsland Road (Kingsland Street, drawn about 40 m off its modern line), Erie Newark Branch, X Ray Stove Polish and La Monte mills (details on sheet 24, part 3), Cathedral, Terrace, Glendale. One part.

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9 of the 1906 Sanborn atlas of Nutley, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. This sheet is turned differently from the northern sheets: Franklin Avenue runs up the left edge and north lies toward the upper left. It covers the south-western part of the town along the Third River and the Belleville boundary. Center street runs along the top of the sheet and Passaic Avenue along the right edge, with Franklin Avenue on the left. Harrison curves from the lower left across the sheet to Passaic Avenue. The land north of Harrison is largely open, with a few dwellings along Center and Passaic Avenue and a compass rose in the middle. The Third River winds from the top of the sheet southwest to the left edge, joined by a tributary from the left; it passes a works of Kirschbaum and Bro., manufacturers of manicure files, on the left edge, whose buildings are marked as having power by gas engine, with coal fires, and fitted with water buckets and fire extinguishers. Franklin Pl., Stager and Ravine Ave. are drawn dashed as proposed streets in the upper left. South of Harrison a small suburban district is laid out in long narrow lots along Entwistle Ave., Gless Ave., Newark Ave., Moore Ave. and Memphis, with frame dwellings built on some, and Meacham Ave. closing the district along the bottom. The boundary of the Township of Belleville crosses this district diagonally as a dash-dot line. The right of way of the East Jersey Water Co. crosses the lower left. Adjoining sheets are numbered 4 and 3 on the left, 11 at the top, 10 on the right and 65 below.
notes: Center is today Centre Street; Moore Ave. is today Moore Place; Passaic Avenue, Franklin Avenue, Harrison Street, Entwistle Avenue, Gless Avenue, Newark Avenue and Meacham Avenue keep their names.
Memphis is printed in two pieces on the same street (the word Memphis low on the street and AVE. farther up); today's street is Memphis Avenue.

Centre Street / Franklin Avenue lies at the top-left corner where both streets are mostly off the sheet; its detected position was about 350 px from where the street edges put it and it was left out of the control.
The control is spread over the whole sheet, but the upper left is held by only one junction (Centre Street / Ravine Avenue); check the seam with sheet 4.
Printed sheet number 9; the scale bar reads 100 feet to one inch.
Scale 100 ft, turned (rotation about -22). Center, Franklin, Harrison, Passaic, Entwistle, Gless, Newark, Moore, Meacham; Centre/Franklin excluded. One part.

sheet-10.description: Sheet 10 of the 1906 Sanborn atlas of Nutley, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, with north toward the upper left. It covers the south-western edge of the town. Passaic Avenue runs down the left side with a long bend, Union Ave. runs down the right side, Cunningham crosses the top and Center crosses the upper third from Passaic Avenue to Union Ave. North of Center, between it and Cunningham, the land is cut into a long row of narrow lots, nearly all vacant; at the left end the greenhouses and sheds of W. L. Jones, florist, are drawn with a note of a pump and windmill, a tank and an artesian well. Miller is a street at the top right, and a few frame dwellings stand along it and on the lots by Union Ave. South of Center a row of houses stands on the narrow lots fronting the street, and a few dwellings line Passaic Avenue. In the middle of the sheet Friedland Road and Hancox are drawn as wide streets running diagonally up to the right, each flanked by closely ruled lots, almost none built on; between them is a large open tract with the compass rose. The lower part is open ground apart from a few houses on Passaic Avenue and Harrison St., which meets Passaic Avenue at the bottom left. The dash-dot boundary of the Township of Belleville crosses the lower part of the sheet. Water pipes of 5 and 6 inches are marked along Passaic Avenue and Center. Adjoining sheets are numbered 17 to the north, 11 and 9 to the west, 15 to the east and 65 and 59 to the south.
notes: Center is today Centre Street; Cunningham and Miller are not in the OpenStreetMap extract under those names and were not used for control.
Hancox is drawn ending short of Passaic Avenue; the modern junction of Hancox Avenue and Passaic Avenue (about 100 m further west) was detected as a false point and excluded.
Friedland Road and Hancox are drawn as wide diagonal streets with lots laid out along them.
Scale 100 ft, rotation about -18. Passaic, Center, Union, Friedland Road, Hancox, Cunningham, Miller. One part.

sheet-11.description: Sheet 11 of the 1906 Sanborn atlas of Nutley, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, with north toward the upper right. It covers the centre of the town south of the Third River's bend: Franklin Ave. runs along the top from the upper left toward the right, Center runs down the left side, Chestnut down the right side and Passaic Ave. along the bottom. In the upper left, William and New run south from Franklin Ave. between blocks of narrow lettered lots, closely built with frame dwellings, and The Franklin Hotel stands at the corner of New and Elm. The Park School Ho., a large brick building drawn in pink, and The Old Homestead School Ho. stand in an open block east of New, with Nutley Town Hall (drawn in pink and housing the Yantacaw Fire Co. and a lock-up) near Chestnut. Church St. enters from the top and Ravine Ave. from the left edge. The Third River crosses the middle of the sheet from the left edge to the right in a wide curve, crossed by Center, Elm and Chestnut. South of the river there is mostly open ground and a large block marked 3; on the left a few buildings stand along Center, including the barrel storage and cooperage of Ed. Ergleson, and near the bottom the Nutley M.E. Church and some houses stand on Passaic Ave., where Cunningham St. and Avondale Rd. join it. Grant Ave. enters Passaic Ave. at the bottom right. A compass rose is in the lower right. Water pipes of 6 and 8 inches are marked in several streets. Adjoining sheets are numbered 5 to the north, 9 and 10 to the west, 12 to the east and 17 to the south.
notes: Center is today Centre Street.
Cunningham Street and Avondale Road are not in the OpenStreetMap extract under those names; they were not used for control.
Chestnut Street / Franklin Avenue (modern) lies about 6 m from where the other junctions place the drawn one and was left out of the control; Chestnut Street / Passaic Avenue was not detected.
The Yantacaw Fire Co. is named on the Nutley Town Hall building.
Scale 100 ft. Franklin, Center, William, New, Church, Chestnut, Passaic, Third River; Park School, Town Hall. One part.

sheet-12.description: Sheet 12 of the 1906 Sanborn atlas of Nutley, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. It covers the western part of the town between Chestnut on the left, Hillside Avenue across the top and Vreeland Avenue on the right, down to Passaic Avenue at the foot. The Third River enters at the left edge near Chestnut and winds across the middle of the sheet before turning south beside Vreeland Avenue. Between Hillside Avenue and Franklin Avenue the blocks are cut into regular narrow house lots, with T. Clements and Son, makers of fancy leather goods, and L. A. Smith's livery stable among the houses. South of Franklin Avenue, Warren and Central Avenue are drawn dashed as proposed streets across empty lots running down to the river. Along the left edge Chestnut is the commercial street: the Central Hotel with a bowling alley, a grocery, a bakery, a barber, a laundry and several shops stand between Hamilton Place and Passaic Avenue, and Bross and Keyser, carpenters and builders, work beside the river. Brookside Avenue, a short lane and Nutley Avenue lead south to Passaic Avenue, which crosses the foot of the sheet; Highfield Lane starts there on sheet 19. The right side, along Vreeland Avenue, holds scattered frame dwellings and the building of The Nutley Sun, with Maple Place laid out near the bottom. Much of the centre and the area near the river is open ground. The compass rose and scale bar are printed on the sheet, and the sheet number 12 is at the upper right, with sheets 5, 6, 11, 13, 17 and 19 numbered at the margins.
notes: Chestnut here is today Chestnut Street; its modern line lies about 3 to 7 m from the drawn centre, so only the Hamilton Place and Passaic Avenue junctions were kept in the control.
Central Avenue and Warren are drawn dashed (proposed); Brookside Avenue and Central Avenue are not in the modern street data.
The Nutley Sun is lettered on a building beside Vreeland Avenue.
Scale 100 ft. Hillside, Franklin, Vreeland, Chestnut, Passaic Aves; Third River; Chestnut Street displaced 4-7 m. One part.

sheet-13.description: Sheet 13 of the 1906 Sanborn atlas of Nutley, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. It covers the area around West Nutley station, from Hillside Avenue across the top to Passaic Avenue near the foot, between Vreeland Avenue on the left and Yantacan Place on the right. The Newark Branch of the Erie Railroad crosses the sheet diagonally from lower left to upper right beside West Nutley Plaza, with a freight house and the West Nutley station on its east side. A building lettered as a bowling establishment and a larger frame building stand on Franklin Avenue near the plaza. Franklin Avenue runs across the upper half with narrow house lots along both sides, and Hawthorn Avenue enters from Hillside Avenue as a short street. East of the railroad the blocks between Elm Place, Yantacaw Place and Broofield Avenue are laid out with dwellings, and The Yantacaw School, a brick building heated by steam and lit by electricity, stands near the right edge. West of the tracks Erie Place is lined with close-set houses on small lots, while the left side of the sheet, between Vreeland Avenue and the railroad, is mostly open land with a few scattered houses and Maple Place laid out across it. The Third River crosses the lower part, with Brook Way running along its north bank and Passaic Avenue on the south, where Satterthwaite Avenue begins. The compass rose and scale bar are printed on the sheet and the sheet number 13 is at the upper left; sheets 7, 12, 14 and 19 are numbered at the margins.
notes: Broofield Avenue is printed as shown; it is today Brookfield Avenue.
Brook Way is today Brookway; Hawthorn Avenue is today Hawthorne Avenue.
The Brookfield Avenue and Yantacaw Place junction was left out of the control as a duplicate of the nearby Erie Place junction.
The street printed Yantacan Place along the right edge continues Yantacaw Place of the modern street data.
Scale 100 ft. West Nutley Plaza and station, Franklin Ave, Yantacaw School, Third River. One part.

sheet-14.description: Sheet 14 of the 1906 Sanborn atlas of Nutley, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. It covers the north-eastern part of the town on both sides of the line between Acquackanonck Township and Passaic County, which runs across the upper part of the sheet. Kingsland Road crosses the middle from left to right, meeting Terrace Avenue, Hillside Avenue, Franklin Avenue, Elm and, at the right edge, Passaic Avenue. North of Kingsland Road the blocks between Terrace Avenue and Passaic Avenue are subdivided into house lots, with Princeton, Newark and the curving Glendale crossing them, and Paterson Avenue running north from Glendale. Most lots are still vacant, and dwellings are scattered, with a denser row of small frame houses along the north side of Kingsland Road. South of Kingsland Road, Franklin Avenue is lined with houses on its east side, and a club house stands near its middle. In the lower left, J. J. Yosseler and Co., makers of pocket books, purses and belts, and St. Paul's Congregational Church stand on Franklin Avenue and Hillside Avenue, and the Newark Branch of the Erie Railroad with the West Nutley freight house and West Nutley Plaza cuts across the lower left corner. The lower right is open land with a few houses and a brick building near the Third River, which flows down the right side to the sheet's lower edge. Yantacaw Place is drawn along the foot. The compass rose and scale bar are printed on the sheet, the sheet number 14 is at the upper right, and sheets 8, 13, 15, 9 and 20 are numbered at the margins.
notes: Kingsland Road is today Kingsland Street on this sheet; Elm is today Elm Place.
Princeton is today Princeton Street; Glendale is today Glendale Street.
Scale 100 ft, rotation about -35. Kingsland Road (Kingsland Street), Terrace, Hillside, Franklin, Elm, Passaic; Acquackanonck Twp / Passaic Co line. One part.

sheet-15.description: Sheet 15 of the 1906 Sanborn atlas of Nutley, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the top of the page, tilted a little to the left. It covers the south-eastern part of the town where it meets the Township of Belleville, whose boundary is drawn as a dash-dot line across the foot of the sheet. Avondale Road bounds the sheet at the top. Miller Street and Union Avenue form one long street along the west side, Center Street crosses the sheet from west to east, and Melrose Avenue, Myrtle Avenue, La Fayette Place and St. Mary's Place run between them. On the east side the double track of the Newark Branch of the Erie Railroad runs diagonally from the top of the sheet to the lower right beside Walnut Street and the curving Washington Avenue; a railroad tower stands on the line near East Center Street. The north-west quarter between Avondale Road, Center Street and Union Avenue is the built-up part, with frame dwellings on narrow lots, H. Hoffmeister Sr.'s dairy farm buildings, and a few outbuildings. Near the railroad stand St. Mary's Lyceum and the brick St. Mary's R. C. Church, the latter coloured as a fireproof building. Much of the middle of the sheet, between Center Street and Hancox Avenue, is open ground with a compass rose, and the blocks along St. Mary's Place and Hancox Avenue are laid out in lots but not built on. A depot or power building of the New Jersey Traction Company is drawn near the foot of the sheet on Washington Avenue. Block numbers 1 to 9 are printed, and the adjoining sheets 10, 16, 17, 18 and 60 are named in the margins.
notes: Avondale Road is today Park Avenue; Melrose Avenue is today Monsignor Owens Place.
Center and East Center Street are today Centre Street and East Centre Street; La Fayette Place is today Lafayette Place; St. Mary's Place is today St Marys Place.
Miller is the northern part of today's Union Avenue; Walnut is today Walnut Street.
The street continuing St. Mary's Place north of Center Street, between block 4 and the railroad, is not named on the sheet.
Scale 100 ft. Union Ave (Miller), Centre St, Hancox, St Marys Pl, Myrtle, Melrose Ave (Monsignor Owens Place), Avondale Road (Park Avenue); Erie Newark Branch. One part.

sheet-16.description: Sheet 16 of the 1906 Sanborn atlas of Nutley, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the top of the page, tilted a little to the left. It covers the south-eastern corner of the town on the west bank of the Passaic River, where the town meets the Township of Belleville, whose boundary is drawn as a dash-dot line across the lower part of the sheet. River Road runs down the east side beside the river, Washington Avenue curves down the west side, and the double track of the Newark Branch of the Erie Railroad runs diagonally beside it. Avondale Road crosses the top of the sheet from Washington Avenue towards the pond, and Hancox Avenue and East Center Street cross the sheet from the west. Most of the ground is open or industrial. The largest area is the Belleville Quarry and Stone Works, with its quarry pond, a second pond with a sluice, scale and powder houses, and industrial tracks that cross the sheet to the river. At River Road the Belleville Quarry and Stone Company has a stone sawing and polishing mill with its own engine, shown with iron-clad walls, and its power, lighting and heating are noted beside it. Two long strips of narrow lots laid out on either side of East Center Street are not yet built on. The American Match Machine Company has a group of brick and frame shops, marked admittance refused, beside the railroad, and two large buildings stand near the Belleville line at the foot of the sheet. A few dwellings stand on River Road. Block numbers 1 to 4 are printed, and the adjoining sheets 15, 21, 42 and 60 are named in the margins.
notes: Avondale Road is probably today Park Avenue; the curve of the drawn road follows it, but the match was not fixed by a junction.
E. Center is today East Centre Street; its junction with Washington Avenue sits about 45 m from where the street is drawn and was left out of the control.
Washington Avenue at Park Avenue is drawn about 14 m from the modern junction and was left out of the control.
Only two junctions (Hancox Avenue / Washington Avenue and East Centre Street / River Road) were used; scale and rotation come from them.
Napoli Alley and Roma Alley do not match modern streets (Humbert Street and Roma Street are nearby but lie tens of metres east).
Scale 100 ft. Washington Ave, Hancox Ave, E. Center St, River Road, Avondale Road; Belleville quarry works and American Match Machine Co. Helmert from two junctions. One part.

sheet-17.description: Sheet 17 of the 1906 Sanborn atlas of Nutley, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. It covers a residential district in the south-west of the town, bounded on the north by Nutley Avenue, on the west by Passaic Avenue, on the south by Avondale Road and Cunningham, and on the east by Myrtle Avenue. Whitford Avenue runs down the sheet from Nutley Avenue to Grant Avenue, and Chestnut and Grant Avenue cross it from west to east. Between Nutley Avenue and Grant Avenue the blocks along Passaic Avenue are the most built up, with J. Stirrat's Nutley Livery stable, a plumber, a tin shop and a row of frame dwellings. A diagonal railroad right of way, with a steel bridge noted at Nutley Avenue, cuts across the north-east corner beside Tennis Place and Nairn Place. East of Whitford Avenue the blocks are largely empty. South of Grant Avenue the long narrow blocks between Hampton Place, Wayne Place, Weston Place and Myrtle Avenue are laid out but almost unbuilt, and a large open block west of Hampton Place holds only a few outbuildings. The Avondale School, a brick building heated by furnace, stands on Passaic Avenue near Avondale Road, and below the road a tract is cut into narrow lots running down to Cunningham. The compass rose and scale bar are printed on the sheet, the sheet number 17 is at the upper left, and sheets 11, 12, 15, 18, 19 and 10 are numbered at the margins.
notes: Avondale Road is today Park Avenue; Weston Place is today Weston Street.
Chestnut is today Chestnut Street; its junction with Passaic Avenue sat about 4 m off and was left out of the control.
The modern Park Avenue and Passaic Avenue junction is realigned against the drawn curve and was left out.
Whitford Avenue is drawn on this sheet only between Nutley Avenue and Grant Avenue; the modern street continues south on a line about 50 m to the west.
A steel bridge is noted where the railroad crosses Nutley Avenue.
Scale 100 ft. Nutley Ave, Whitford, Grant, Avondale Road (Park Avenue), Passaic Ave. One part.

sheet-18.description: Sheet 18 of the 1906 Sanborn atlas of Nutley, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. It lies south-east of sheet 17 in the south-western part of the town and covers the blocks between Avondale Road on the left and Nutley Avenue on the right, from Whitford Avenue at the top to Washington Avenue at the foot. Grant Avenue runs down the middle of the sheet and Chestnut parallel to it on the right, while Hampton Place, Wayne Place, Weston Place, Myrtle Avenue, Walnut and Washington Avenue cross at intervals. A railroad right of way, the Newark branch, crosses the sheet diagonally from lower left to upper right, passing through the Grant Avenue and Myrtle Avenue crossing and close to Nairn Place. Most of the blocks hold scattered one- and two-storey frame dwellings on large lots, with the Grace Episcopal Church near the top of Grant Avenue and Avondale Fire Station No. 2, with hose and ladder truck and two horses, on Hampton Place. Along the railroad stand J. Hawkins's coal and wood yard and Jacob Kol's greenhouses, and in the lower left corner the Imperial Cutlery Works, Hirsch and Son managers, is drawn in detail with a note on its power, heating and fire protection. Several streets, among them Durant Place, Burnett Place and Stockton Place, are short and run only part way across their blocks. The compass rose and scale bar are printed on the sheet, the sheet number 18 is at the upper right, and sheets 15, 17, 19, 21 and 22 are numbered at the margins.
notes: Avondale Road is today Park Avenue; Weston Place is today Weston Street.
Walnut is today Walnut Street; Chestnut is today Chestnut Street.
The Park Avenue junctions with Washington Avenue and Walnut Street sat 3 to 5 m off the fit where Avondale Road curves, and were left out of the control.
The Imperial Cutlery Works carries a printed note on its power, heating and fire protection.
Scale 100 ft. Grant Ave, Myrtle, Walnut, Washington, Nutley Ave, Erie Newark Branch. One part.

sheet-19.description: Sheet 19 of the 1906 Sanborn atlas of Nutley, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. It covers the area around Nutley station, between Nutley Avenue on the left and the open ground east of Satterthwaite Avenue, from Passaic Avenue across the top to Walnut at the foot. The Newark Branch of the Erie Railroad crosses the sheet diagonally from lower left to upper right, with the Nutley railroad station and a building lettered for the Nutley Realty Co. beside it, and the Nutley Field Club house on the west side. Passaic Avenue runs along the top and meets Brookfield Avenue and Vreeland Avenue near the upper edge, while Whitford Avenue, Tennis Place and Walnut cross the sheet from side to side. Highfield Lane and Satterthwaite Avenue run down the middle; the blocks between them are laid out in long narrow lots, with scattered frame dwellings. West of Highfield Lane, between Nutley Avenue and the lane, the lots are partly built over with small houses. The eastern part is largely vacant: large blocks marked with dashed lines for a Proposed Street run diagonally across it, a narrow lane runs beside the right edge, and North Road crosses the lower right past a short row of houses on Rutgers Place. The compass rose and scale bar are printed on the sheet, the sheet number 19 is at the upper left, and sheets 12, 13, 17, 18, 20 and 22 are numbered at the margins.
notes: Walnut is today Walnut Street; Highfield Lane keeps its name on the modern map.
Proposed Street is drawn dashed; it is not built on this sheet.
The Nutley Avenue and Walnut Street junction lies at the bottom edge and sat about 5 m off the fit, so it was left out of the control.
The Nutley Avenue and Passaic Avenue junction was rejected, 15 m off the fit.
Scale 100 ft. Nutley station, Highfield Lane, Satterthwaite Ave, Passaic Ave, North Road. One part.

sheet-20.description: Sheet 20 of the 1906 Sanborn atlas of Nutley, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. It covers the north-eastern edge of the town, where Nutley meets Passaic County, whose boundary with Acquackanonck Township is drawn as a dash-dot line down the right side of the sheet. Passaic Avenue crosses the top, Kingsland Road runs down the east side from the junction with Passaic Avenue, and Washington Avenue crosses the foot of the sheet. The middle of the sheet is taken up by the Third River, which enters at the top and widens into Kingsland Pond, a long narrow pond that runs south-east to a dam and sluice beside Kingsland Road. Almost all of the ground is open. Short streets are laid out and named but not built on: Glendale Street and Newark Avenue at the top right, North Road and Roosevelt Street in the lower left, a street marked Proposed Street at the left edge, and the strip of Rutgers Place at the left. Walnut is drawn only with dashed lines as a proposed street. The few buildings are dwellings and outbuildings along Kingsland Road, a group of frame farm buildings near the pond that includes a pink-coloured building, and the Hotel Feuerbach, whose frame hotel with bowling alley, dining room and summer kitchen is drawn at the head of Roosevelt Street with sheds, lit by kerosene and heated by steam. A pipeline right of way of the Jersey City Water Supply Company crosses the foot of the sheet diagonally. Block numbers 2 to 4 and 9 to 11 are printed, and the adjoining sheets 3, 13, 14, 19, 22, 23 and 24 are named in the margins.
notes: Kingsland Road is today Kingsland Street from Passaic Avenue to the pond and Kingsland Road south of it.
Glendale St. is printed Glendale Street; today Glendale Street meets Passaic Avenue near the drawn junction.
Roosevelt is today Roosevelt Street; Washington Avenue and North Road keep their names.
The street at the left edge printed Lane follows the line of today's Rutgers Place; its first letters are not legible.
The junctions of Roosevelt Street with Washington Avenue and with North Road sit 6 to 8 m off the fit of the Passaic Avenue junctions; the fit is a compromise, low to medium confidence.
Right of way of the Jersey City Water Supply Company is lettered across the foot of the sheet.
Scanned at lower resolution than the other sheets (7400 px wide), so the fitted scale is about 3.44 px per foot at 100 feet to an inch.

Roosevelt Street junctions disagreed with the Passaic Avenue junctions by about 2 degrees and up to 13 m against sheet 23; the sheet is placed from the three Passaic Avenue junctions only (low confidence).

Scale 100 ft, but scanned at lower resolution (7400 px wide against about 8450): fitted 3.44 px/ft. The second pass recognises the rescan and normalises it (the earlier scale_ft 115 workaround was removed, 2026-11-21). Passaic Ave, Kingsland Road, Third River and Kingsland Pond, North Road, Roosevelt, Washington Ave; White Spring Paper Co at the east edge (details on sheet 24, part 1). One part.

sheet-21.description: Sheet 21 of the 1906 Sanborn atlas of Nutley, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the top of the page, tilted a little to the left. It covers the north-eastern corner of the town on the west bank of the Passaic River, across which lies Bergen County. Nutley Avenue crosses the top of the sheet, Grant Avenue crosses it a little below the middle, and Washington Avenue runs down the west side. River Road runs down the east side beside the river and is joined near the bottom by a road to a steel draw bridge over the Passaic River; Avondale Road leaves Washington Avenue at the foot of the sheet and curves towards River Road around Quarry Pond. Most of the ground is open. Large blocks between Nutley Avenue and Grant Avenue and between Grant Avenue and the bottom have only a few scattered frame dwellings and outbuildings. The built-up part lies in the lower left, where narrow lots between Washington Avenue and Roma Alley are lined with small frame dwellings, stores and sheds, with Napoli Alley and Roma Alley running between them. Gorman's Hotel stands on Washington Avenue at Grant Avenue, and the River Road Hotel stands on River Road. Several houses and a pink-coloured building stand at the foot of the sheet near Avondale Road and the pond. A compass rose is drawn in the open ground at the top. The adjoining sheets 15, 16, 18 and 22 are named in the margins, and block numbers 1 to 3 are printed.
notes: Avondale Road is probably today Park Avenue, on the line of the curving road at the foot of the sheet.
Only Washington Avenue junctions (with Nutley Avenue, Grant Avenue and Park Avenue) were used as control; the sheet is placed from them with a Helmert transformation, low confidence.
Today's River Road sits 6 to 14 m from where it is drawn and the Nutley Avenue and Grant Avenue junctions with it were left out of the control.
The distances along Washington Avenue fit about 4.1 pixels per foot, about 5 percent larger than the scale bar suggests.
Napoli Alley and Roma Alley do not match modern streets.
Scale 100 ft (drawn about 4-5 percent large along Washington Ave). Nutley Ave, Grant Ave, Washington Ave, River Road, Passaic River; helmert from three hand-picked Washington Ave junctions. One part.

sheet-22.description: Sheet 22 of the 1906 Sanborn atlas of Nutley, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned on the page, with north toward the upper right. It covers the north-eastern edge of the town beside the Passaic River, with the river and Bergen County at the foot of the sheet. Washington Avenue, 100 feet wide, crosses the sheet from left to right, with Walnut running parallel above it; Nutley Avenue runs down the left edge, and River Road runs along the foot of the sheet beside the river. Above Washington Avenue lie two blocks, numbered 8 and 9, laid out with lots, between Nutley Avenue, Highfield Lane and Satterthwaite Avenue, and a large block 10 beyond with the dashed lines of the proposed Walnut. Below Washington Avenue the land is almost empty. Highfield Lane, Satterthwaite Avenue and Conduit Place are drawn with dashed lines as proposed streets, and a short Lane runs off to the left. A few dwellings stand along Nutley Avenue and in the blocks, a laboratory and a shed stand beside Conduit Place, and the larger works of the right half, a group of frame buildings and a large house with outbuildings, are drawn between a second Lane and Rembrandt Avenue, with a note of a water tank of 10000 gallons on a stone foundation. Rembrandt Avenue bends towards River Road. A pipeline right of way of the Jersey City Water Supply Company crosses the lower right corner. A compass rose with the north arrow is drawn beside Washington Avenue. Block numbers 4 to 10 are printed, and the adjoining sheets 18, 19, 20, 21 and 23 are named in the margins.
notes: Walnut is today Walnut Street; Highfield Lane and Satterthwaite Avenue keep their names north of Washington Avenue.
South of Washington Avenue Highfield Lane and Satterthwaite Avenue are drawn dashed and offset to the left of their northern parts; the modern line was used only north of Washington Avenue.
River Road is not used as control: a hand-picked Nutley Avenue / River Road junction sat about 14 m off the rest of the fit, as on sheet 21.
Rembrandt Avenue is not in the modern street data.
Right of way of the Jersey City Water Supply Company is lettered across the lower right corner.
Scale 100 ft, rotation about 73. Walnut, Washington Ave, Nutley Ave, Highfield Lane, Satterthwaite Ave; control only near Washington Ave. One part.

sheet-23.description: Sheet 23 of the 1906 Sanborn atlas of Nutley, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned on the page, with north toward the upper right. It covers the far north-eastern corner of the town where the Passaic River and the Third River meet, with the line between Nutley and Acquackanonck Township, Passaic County, running diagonally up the right half. Washington, 100 feet wide, crosses the top of the sheet and is met by Roosevelt, and River Road runs across the lower part of the sheet from the left edge to the right. Rembrandt Avenue comes down the left side, a Lane runs south from Washington near the middle, and Kingsland Road runs down the right side from the top right corner to River Road. The sheet is largely open land. A pipeline right of way of the Jersey City Water Supply Company crosses it diagonally from the lower left to the upper right. Between River Road and Kingsland Road lie large unbuilt blocks laid out with lot lines, and a few frame outbuildings and a flat stand beside Kingsland Road. The Essex Hotel, a frame hotel with sheds and a barn, stands on River Road beside the Lane, with notes that it has no watchman and is lit by kerosene. At the foot of the sheet a large frame house and outbuildings stand beside the Passaic River, and at the lower right The Waldrich Bleachery, drawn in pink with a note that admittance is refused, stands on the Third River below a ravine. Block numbers 1 and 4 are printed, and the adjoining sheets 20 and 22 are named in the margins.
notes: Roosevelt is today Roosevelt Street; Washington is today Washington Avenue.
Only two junctions were used (Roosevelt Street / Washington Avenue and Kingsland Road / River Road); scale and rotation come from them, low confidence.
Rembrandt Avenue and the Lane are not in the modern street data.
Right of way of the Jersey City Water Supply Company is lettered across the sheet.
A date, 11-9-05, is written in the lower right corner.
Scale 100 ft, rotation about 73. Washington, Roosevelt, River Road, Kingsland Road, Essex Hotel, Waldrich Bleachery; helmert from two junctions. One part.

sheet-24-1.description: Left and largest part of sheet 24 of the 1906 Sanborn atlas of Nutley, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and separated from the other two parts by heavy lines. It enlarges the mills on the Third River where Kingsland Road crosses the line between Essex and Passaic counties, at the eastern edge of the town in the area of sheet 20. Kingsland Road runs down the left side, with the county line drawn diagonally beside it. The main works are those of the White Spring Paper Company, W. H. Shurtleff manager, makers of white tissue paper: a large group of frame and brick buildings holding a beating engine room, rag storage, draining room, bleach room, paper machine room, dynamo and engine rooms, a machine shop, a boiler house with three boilers and a paper finishing and storage building, with a stone and brick white paper and cotton rag storage building and two hose houses to the north. A long note gives the watchman, steam and electric power, coal fuel, electric light, water supply, hose and pumps. East of it stand the frame buildings of the Meers Artificial Leather Company, with curing, coating and varnish mixing rooms. A tail race runs east across the part above the mills and the Third River below them. North of the works is a group of frame buildings beside Kingsland Road, and to the south a few scattered dwellings and sheds. A compass rose and the sheet numbers 20 and 0 are drawn in the margins.
notes: Placed from four building corners carried from sheet 20 (no street junction on this part); sheet 20 itself rests on five points with a leave-one-out error of about 10 m, so this part is low confidence.

Scale 50 ft. Three parts: part 1 (left, largest) White Spring Paper Co and Meers Artificial Leather Co on the Third River at Kingsland Road and the Passaic County line (area of sheet 20); part 2 (inset, top right) Dalton Pouncing Paper Co on Bloomfield Ave at Kingsland Road; part 3 (lower right) Ray Stove Polish Co and Geo. La Monte & Son safety paper mill by the Erie Newark Branch, Kingsland Road and Cedar (area of sheet 8).

sheet-24-2.description: Inset in the upper right corner of sheet 24 of the 1906 Sanborn atlas of Nutley, drawn at 50 feet to an inch within a heavy frame and turned like the rest of the atlas, with north toward the upper right. It shows the works of the Dalton Pouncing Paper Company on the north side of Bloomfield Avenue just west of Kingsland Road, in the north-eastern part of the town covered at smaller scale by sheets 2 and 8. The works consist of a long two-storey frame building used for belt pouncing and sandpaper finishing and for storage, with a small brick building and a frame shed beside it; the notes record no watchman, power and light by electricity, heating by stove, water from a well and twelve water buckets as the only fire appliances. One other small frame building stands near the western edge of the inset. The rest of the frame is open ground, with the property line drawn around the works and the words no exposure along its northern side. Bloomfield Avenue runs along the bottom of the inset and Kingsland Road along its right side, where the tracks of the Newark Branch of the Erie Railroad cross the corner of the junction diagonally. A small north arrow is drawn in the open ground west of the works, and a hydrant is marked on Bloomfield Avenue.
notes: Kingsland Road here is today Kingsland Street, whose modern line is about 40 m from the drawn road (see sheet 8), so the modern junction was not used.

Placed from two corners of the Bloomfield Avenue / Kingsland Road junction carried from sheet 8 and a derived point 300 ft west along Bloomfield Avenue; scale held at 50 feet to an inch. Low to medium confidence.

Scale 50 ft. Three parts: part 1 (left, largest) White Spring Paper Co and Meers Artificial Leather Co on the Third River at Kingsland Road and the Passaic County line (area of sheet 20); part 2 (inset, top right) Dalton Pouncing Paper Co on Bloomfield Ave at Kingsland Road; part 3 (lower right) Ray Stove Polish Co and Geo. La Monte & Son safety paper mill by the Erie Newark Branch, Kingsland Road and Cedar (area of sheet 8).

sheet-24-3.description: Lower right part of sheet 24 of the 1906 Sanborn atlas of Nutley, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and separated from the rest of the sheet by heavy lines. It enlarges the industrial strip between a pond on the Third River and Kingsland Road, north of Cedar, in the area of sheet 8. At the top stand the brick and frame buildings of the X Ray Stove Polish Company, makers of stove polish: storage and finishing rooms, a mixing and milling room, an engine and boiler house, and a fire-proof storage building of steel and cement construction. Below them the double tracks of the Newark Branch of the Erie Railroad cross the part diagonally. South of the railroad is the paper pouncing mill of George La Monte and Son, makers of safety paper, with a long brick storage building, the mill itself and a small yellow outbuilding, with a long note on its watchman, power, light and fire appliances. The Third River and the pond outflow wind through the open ground on the west, and a narrow stream runs south past the La Monte mill. Kingsland Road runs down the right edge and Cedar along the bottom. A scale of feet is drawn at the foot of the sheet.
notes: Kingsland Road here is today Kingsland Street, but its modern line is about 40 m from the drawn road (sheet 8), so it was not used.
Placed from five building corners carried from sheet 8 (X Ray Stove Polish Co. and the La Monte storage building); low to medium confidence.

Scale 50 ft. Three parts: part 1 (left, largest) White Spring Paper Co and Meers Artificial Leather Co on the Third River at Kingsland Road and the Passaic County line (area of sheet 20); part 2 (inset, top right) Dalton Pouncing Paper Co on Bloomfield Ave at Kingsland Road; part 3 (lower right) Ray Stove Polish Co and Geo. La Monte & Son safety paper mill by the Erie Newark Branch, Kingsland Road and Cedar (area of sheet 8).
